title: Telemetry retention tiering and operator handoff playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary

This playbook defines the telemetry retention tiering strategy for private (VPC / on‑prem) deployments and the operator handoff procedures required to ensure legal/compliance evidence can be produced with minimal operational impact. It balances three constraints: regulatory evidence preservation, day‑to‑day operator cost, and customer privacy expectations.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to all private deployments managed by the Redwood Operator (VPC and air‑gapped on‑prem packages).
- Covers telemetry types: control plane audit logs, runtime request traces (sampling), model KV/cache telemetry, billing/usage counters, and operator debug traces.
- Does NOT change customer application data retention (customer data stored by tenants) — that is governed by the tenant contract.

Owners and escalation

- Primary owner: Private Deployments SRE (team alias: eng-private-sre@redwood.example.com)
- Secondary owner: Privacy & Compliance (privacy@redwood.example.com)
- Oncall escalation: follow Team SRE oncall matrix; page: /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-and-escalation

Retention tiering model (policy overview)

We classify telemetry into three retention tiers. Each tier has retention duration, sampling or aggregation prescription, and evidence packaging expectations.

1) Tier A — Forensic evidence (Audit + Customer incident)
   - Purpose: Preserve full-fidelity records required for legal/regulatory investigation or contractual SLA disputes.
   - Retention: 365 days (default) for regulated customers; configurable down to 180 days for non‑regulated.
   - Sampling: full capture where possible (no sampling of control plane audit entries).
   - Storage: encrypted at rest with customer‑bound KMS key when configured; HSM-backed sealing for air‑gapped customers.

2) Tier B — Operational diagnostics
   - Purpose: Day‑2 troubleshooting, performance regression analysis, and moderately detailed traces.
   - Retention: 90 days.
   - Sampling: event sampling at 5–10% for high‑volume request traces, 100% for operator-initiated debug sessions tagged as "debug-session".
   - Aggregation: rolling 1‑minute histograms for latency distributions beyond 7 days.

3) Tier C — Aggregate metrics and long-term cost profile
   - Purpose: Cost analysis, capacity planning, ML quality monitoring (high-level).
   - Retention: 24 months for aggregated metrics; raw traces not stored.
   - Sampling: aggregated only (e.g., per‑route token counts, 1h granularity).

Retention table (reference)

| Telemetry type | Retention tier | Default retention | Sampling / aggregation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Control plane audit (auth, config changes) | Tier A | 365d | 100% (immutable append) |
| Operator session recordings (kubectl/ssh proxy) | Tier A | 365d | 100% (encrypted) |
| Runtime request traces (per-token / per-request) | Tier B | 90d | 5–10% head sampling; debug-session override |
| KV-cache change logs | Tier A | 365d | 100% until snapshotting completes |
| Cost & billing metrics | Tier C | 730d | aggregated hourly rollups |
| Model correctness evals / regression alerts | Tier C | 730d | point-in-time artifacts stored (not raw logs) |

Policy details and thresholds

- Storage threshold guard: when Tier A store grows > 80% of allocated customer quota, trigger notice to customer operator and start oldest-first cold archive (7‑day delay required).
- Cold archive SLA: archive operations must complete within 72 hours of trigger; indexing metadata retained online for 180 days.
- Owner must configure per-customer quota at onboarding; suggested default quotas: 500GB Tier A, 200GB Tier B, 10GB Tier C aggregated index.

Operator handoff checklist (pre‑handoff)

Before handing a private deployment to field operators, complete the following:

1) Telemetry contract signoff
   - Confirm customer has signed telemetry retention SLA and encryption/KMS preferences.
   - Verify required compliance clauses (e.g., EU‑FinServ, HIPAA) are enumerated in the onboarding ticket.
2) Quota and tier mapping
   - Apply per‑tenant quotas. Document in handoff sheet: tenant_id, Tier A quota, Tier B quota, archive bucket ID.
3) Evidence export & replay sanity check
   - Run the evidence export rehearsal (see Procedure: Evidence export below). Verify export checksum and that index files open.
4) Emergency-access escrow
   - Ensure emergency access procedures and escrow keys exist and are logged with Security.

Operator handoff checklist (operator acceptance) — operator must confirm:

- They can run export/replay procedure (steps 1–6 in Evidence export).
- They understand alarm thresholds and how to pause sampling for privacy requests.
- Contact points and ticketing priority for regulated evidence requests are known.

Procedure: Evidence export (for an incident or legal request)

The following numbered procedure produces an evidence bundle that preserves chain-of-custody metadata. Operators must follow exactly.

Prereqs: operator CLI access (role: telemetry-exporter), customer consent record (SLA ID), KMS access (if customer uses customer-managed keys).

1) Create a short-lived export token (valid 24h):
   - CLI: redwoodctl telemetry auth create-token --tenant <TENANT_ID> --purpose "evidence-export" --ttl 24h
2) Lock writes to Tier A indices to preserve snapshot consistency:
   - CLI: redwoodctl telemetry lock-indices --tenant <TENANT_ID> --indices tierA --reason "evidence export <CASE_ID>"
3) Run export and sign with operator key:
   - CLI: redwoodctl telemetry export --tenant <TENANT_ID> --since 2026-05-01 --until 2026-05-14 --indices tierA,tierB --out /tmp/evidence-<CASE_ID>.tar.gz
   - Signing: cosign sign --key /ops/keys/operator-signer.key /tmp/evidence-<CASE_ID>.tar.gz
4) Generate metadata manifest (SHA256) and append provenance:
   - CLI: sha256sum /tmp/evidence-<CASE_ID>.tar.gz > /tmp/evidence-<CASE_ID>.sha256
   - Create manifest.json (fields: case_id, tenant_id, exporter, export_time, indices, signed_by) — save alongside bundle.
5) Upload to evidence store (encrypted at rest)
   - CLI: redwoodctl telemetry upload-evidence --file /tmp/evidence-<CASE_ID>.tar.gz --manifest /tmp/evidence-<CASE_ID>.sha256 --store-id evidence://redwood-secure/<TENANT_ID>/<CASE_ID>
   - Note: For air‑gapped customers, follow offline courier workflow (see Appendix B).
6) Unlock indices once upload confirms checksum and manifest match.

Audit and chain-of-custody notes

- All export operations are logged to the Control Plane Audit (Tier A) and must not be deleted for 730 days.
- Signing must use operator key stored in the org’s HSM and rotated per key‑rotation policy.
- For any copy leaving customer boundary (e.g., courier), the operator must produce a signed transfer manifest and retain transport receipts.

Sampling management and runtime controls

- Dynamic sampling API: operators may adjust trace sampling with a rate policy scoped by route and tenant:

  Example API call:
  curl -X POST 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPERATOR_TOKEN" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    https://private-controlplane.internal/api/v1/tenants/<TENANT_ID>/sampling 
    -d '{"route":"/generate","sample_rate":0.05,"expires_at":"2026-07-01T00:00:00Z"}'

- Default safety: sampling adjustments that increase disk consumption by >25% in 24h are rate‑limited and require approver signoff from Private Deployments SRE.

Change control and rollback considerations

- Changes to retention tiers (e.g., reducing Tier A duration) require:
  1) Customer consent (signed change request),
  2) A rollback plan for preserved evidence to be moved to cold archive (if decreasing retention), and
  3) A 14‑day notice window (automated by onboarding system).

- Rollback of telemetry ingestion pipelines must preserve last 7 days of data in a hot buffer to avoid gaps. Rolling configuration steps:
  1) Stage new pipeline config in staging cluster.
  2) Run synthetic traffic against sampling policy.
  3) Promote and monitor for 24h; if disk pressure > 70% or increase in error-rate > 0.5%, rollback.

SLOs and alerting thresholds (operational)

- Evidence export success rate: 100% for export jobs initiated by operator within 72h SLA. Missed SLA is a Sev2 incident.
- Sampling controller availability: 99.95% monthly uptime.
- Storage overutilization alert: trigger at 75% of per-tenant Tier A quota (pager to eng-private-sre).
- Cold-archive lag alert: trigger when an archive job exceeds 72h.

Cost and sizing guidance (practical examples)

- Typical per-customer daily ingestion (estimates):
  - Small tenant (low QPS): 50–200MB/day (Tier B heavy traces disabled)
  - Medium tenant (20qps sustained): 600MB–2GB/day
  - Large regulated tenant (high QPS, Tier A enabled): 5–20GB/day

- Cost estimate model (US region):
  - Hot Tier A storage: $0.12/GB/month
  - Warm Tier B storage (90d): $0.06/GB/month
  - Cold archive: $0.01/GB/month + retrieval fees

Onboarding checklist snippet (to include in handoff doc)

- Confirm signed telemetry SLA and KMS preference.
- Assign Tier quotas in provisioning manifest.
- Run export rehearsal and attach manifest to onboarding ticket.
- Confirm operator acceptance and runbook location.

Appendix A — Example retention YAML (operator editable)

retention_policies:
  - name: tierA-audit
    retention_days: 365
    indices: ["controlplane-audit", "operator-sessions", "kv-change-log"]
    encryption: "customer-managed-kms"
  - name: tierB-traces
    retention_days: 90
    sampling_rate: 0.05
    aggregation: "1m-histogram-after-7d"
  - name: tierC-aggregates
    retention_days: 730
    aggregation: "hourly-rollups"

Appendix B — Air‑gapped / courier evidence workflow

- For customers with no egress, follow the air‑gapped courier protocol:
  1) Generate encrypted evidence bundle per Evidence export procedure.
  2) Copy to signed USB devices that meet FIPS 140‑2 Level 3 (operator compliance).
  3) Produce a signed transfer manifest and get two operator signatures.
  4) Hand over to customer rep and retain a signed receipt.
